# 1. Introduction

This project looks at how daily screen time and social media platform are associated with sleep, anxiety (GAD-7) and depression (PHQ-9) in adults.
The results are statistical associations, not causal effects and not a diagnosis.

Data: adult survey dataset in `data/alternative_dataset.csv` (add citation here).

Run this file from top to bottom. Scripts live in `src/`.

# 2. Analysis (adult data)

We fit a linear regression for sleep duration, GAD-7 and PHQ-9, with daily screen time as the predictor, adjusted for age, gender, late-night use, social comparison and activity type. Confidence intervals are heteroskedasticity-robust (HC3).

```{r analysis}
source("src/analysis.R")
results <- run_analysis("data/alternative_dataset.csv")
results$plots$effects
results$plots$sleep
```

```{r interpretation, echo=FALSE}
eff <- results$screen_effects
get <- function(o, col) round(eff[[col]][eff$outcome == o], 2)
```

**Interpretation.** After adjusting for age, gender, late-night use, social comparison and activity type, one additional hour of daily screen time is associated with a difference of
`r get("Sleep_Duration_Hours", "estimate")` hours of sleep
(95% CI `r get("Sleep_Duration_Hours", "conf_low")` to `r get("Sleep_Duration_Hours", "conf_high")`),
`r get("GAD_7_Score", "estimate")` GAD-7 points
(95% CI `r get("GAD_7_Score", "conf_low")` to `r get("GAD_7_Score", "conf_high")`) and
`r get("PHQ_9_Score", "estimate")` PHQ-9 points
(95% CI `r get("PHQ_9_Score", "conf_low")` to `r get("PHQ_9_Score", "conf_high")`).
Intervals that include 0 mean we cannot distinguish the association from no association.
These are observational associations, not causal effects, and the held-out validation shows how much of the variation the model actually predicts.

# 3. App

The app uses a simpler model than the analysis above: `outcome ~ daily screen time + platform`, with no other covariates, so that users can see differences between platforms.
Its numbers are therefore not expected to match the adjusted estimates in section 2.

The Shiny app lets users enter their platform(s) and screen time and see predictions.
Run this chunk manually (it opens the app; stop it before continuing).

```{r app, eval=FALSE}
shiny::runApp("src")
```
